jobs.title: Private Wealth, Investment Manager
jobs.description:
As a Private Wealth, Investment Manager , you will be responsible for helping Citizens team win new assets under management by assisting the team in bringing in new high net worth and institutional clients and identifying new opportunities with existing clients, through advising on investment solutions. The Private Wealth Investment Manager is the senior, client facing investment expert in the local market.

Primary responsibilities include
- Responsible for the completion of the investment policy statement and determining the appropriate investment solutions based upon client’s profile and constraints, including manager selection and type of vehicle.
- Responsible for ongoing client communication, including active market updates and portfolio performance assessments.
- Meet with clients to review investment performance and forecast market changes based on economic and industry analysis, including objectives and asset allocation models, ensuring current allocations are appropriate.
- Develop and recommend strategies to achieve the investment goals of client.

Qualifications, Education, Certifications and/or Other Professional Credentials
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field
- 7+ years of wealth management, investment advisory, or financial services experience working with investment products and high-net-worth clients
- Series 7 and Series 63/65 or 66 licenses required and in good standing
- Professional designation preferred (CFA, CFP, CRPC, or similar)
- Experience working within a Registered Investment Advisor (RIA) environment or partnering with RIAs preferred, with an understanding of fiduciary investment management, portfolio construction, and client advisory best practices.
Strong knowledge of alternative investments, including private equity, private credit, hedge funds, real assets, and other non-traditional investment strategies.
- Strong analytical, quantitative, and investment research capabilities
- Experience evaluating portfolio performance, developing investment recommendations, and supporting financial planning strategies
- Exceptional relationship management and client service skills, with the ability to build trust and credibility with ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families
- Strong communication and presentation skills, including the ability to explain complex investment concepts in a clear and client-friendly manner
- High attention to detail, sound judgment, and a commitment to delivering a personalized, white-glove client experience
- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining responsiveness, professionalism, and discretion with sensitive client matters

Hours & Work Schedule
- Hours per Week: 40
- Work Schedule: Monday-Friday

jobs.title: Finance Director - Credit Card & Unsecured Lending
jobs.description:
CFO – Credit Card & Unsecured Lending
Position Summary
Citizens is seeking a dynamic Finance Director (SVP) to serve as the CFO and strategic finance leader for the Credit Card and Unsecured Lending businesses. This role will partner directly with Consumer Lending leadership, Product, Risk, Treasury, Marketing, Operations, and Enterprise Finance leaders to drive business performance, profitable growth, and strategic decision-making.
The position is responsible for financial leadership across Citizens' Credit Card and Unsecured Lending portfolios, including business planning, forecasting, profitability, pricing analytics, balance sheet management, credit performance oversight, capital optimization, and executive reporting. The successful candidate will act as a trusted advisor to senior business leaders while helping shape the near- and long-term growth strategy of one of Citizens' priority Consumer Lending businesses.
Key Responsibilities
Business CFO Leadership
- Serve as the primary Finance executive supporting Credit Card and Unsecured Lending leadership - acting as the key advisor for executive decision making, investment prioritization, and business performance management.
- Lead financial strategy development and support achievement of growth, profitability, and customer objectives.
- Develop and deliver materials for executive management, forecasting reviews, strategic planning sessions, and board-level discussions.

Financial Planning & Analysis
- Own monthly, annual, and strategic plan forecasting processes for Balance Sheet, Income Statement, and non-financial outlooks.
- Identify risks and opportunities and develop actions to close forecast gaps.
- Drive portfolio profitability analysis across products, customer segments, acquisition channels, and vintages.
- Partner with Product, Strategy, and Marketing teams to evaluate customer & relationship and product economics .
- Partner with Credit Risk to evaluate portfolio performance, loss trends, and risk-adjusted returns.
- Partner with Treasury and Finance leadership on funding, interest rate sensitivity, and balance sheet strategies.
- Monitor performance against profitability, capital, and return objectives.

Leadership & Organizational Development
- Lead analysts and finance managers supporting Credit Card and Unsecured Lending while building and developing a high-performing Card and Unsecured finance team as Citizens undergoes our "Reimagine the Bank" initiatives.
- Drive process automation, reporting modernization, and data-driven decision making.
- Foster strong partnership across Consumer Lending, Enterprise Finance, Treasury, Risk, and Corporate FP&A.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or related field.
- Progressive finance experience within banking or financial services.
- Experience leading and developing finance teams.
- Demonstrated experience supporting consumer lending, consumer banking, credit card, payments, personal lending, or retail banking businesses.
- Strong skills in: - Financial planning & forecasting
- Profitability analysis
- Executive communication
- Financial modeling
- Strategic business case development

- Proven ability to influence senior executives and cross-functional leadership teams.

Preferred Qualifications
-  CFA, CPA, or other advanced financial designation.
- Experience with Essbase, Tableau, Dodeca, SQL-based reporting, and financial planning systems.

Hours & Work Schedule
- Hours per Week: 40+
- Schedule: Monday through Friday (4 days in office required, 1 day remote)

Work Authorization:
This role is not eligible for new employer sponsored or current H-1 B visa holders. Applicants, including current OPT, L and other visa holders, must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for new employer sponsorship for themselves or their spouses now and in the future.

jobs.title: Analyst II Investment Banking (Corporate Finance)
jobs.description:
Citizens is seeking an ambitious Investment Banking Analyst to join our Investment Banking team in Charlotte covering the Industrials sectors. The Investment Banking Analyst will be involved in all facets of Citizens’ investment banking activities and will play an integral role supporting the origination and execution of a broad range of transactions, including private and public financings (equity, equity-linked and debt), mergers and acquisitions and other advisory services.
Primary responsibilities include
The responsibilities of the Analyst include, but are not limited to, financial analysis and modeling, conducting industry and company-specific research, coordinating the various processes involved in a financing or sale, and the preparation of pitch materials, client presentations, offering memoranda, proposals, and other written materials for meetings with clientele. Citizens offers junior banking professionals the opportunity to work closely with senior bankers and have direct interaction with current and prospective clients within Citizens’ coverage universe.
Qualifications, Education, Certifications and/or Other Professional Credentials
- 1 year of related experience in M&A, Corporate Finance, Industry Coverage, Leveraged Finance / Capital Markets, Equity Research, or Buyside Equities
- Industry knowledge and transaction experience within the Industrials sectors is strongly preferred.
- Skills with the ability to express ideas in a persuasive, organized, and articulate manner.
- Ability to function as part of a flat organization, manage several projects at once and work effectively as an individual and as part of multiple teams.
- Demonstrated aptitude for quantitative and qualitative analysis with a solid understanding of financial statements, financial modeling and company or industry analysis.
- Self-starting team player who can think strategically and excel in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, challenging work environment.
- High degree of maturity and integrity with a positive and hardworking attitude.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Full command of Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
- Experience with related financial services software including S&P CapitalIQ, S&P Leveraged Commentary, Advantage Data, Bloomberg, Thomson One, Thomson Loan Pricing Connector, FactSet, etc.

jobs.title: Investment Banking Associate - Debt Capital Markets
jobs.description:
Citizens is seeking an experienced Debt Capital Markets Associate to support the aligned industry team. This position offers an excellent opportunity for you to join a rapidly growing investment banking platform with market leading positions in middle market corporate and sponsor backed transactions complemented by strong public equity research. As part of our team, you’re made ready for a fulfilling career with exciting new challenges and opportunities to stretch yourself!
While in this role, you will be significantly involved in transactions from origination through closing. Additionally, you should have the ability to work on multiple projects and transactions concurrently. Furthermore, you will play a critical role on deal terms and coordinating projects and will interact directly with managing directors, senior management, other groups within Citizens, client management terms, private equity firms, legal counsel, and professionals at other banks.

Primary responsibilities include
- Working with Managing Directors to develop new business ideas, pitch strategies or transaction financing scenarios to help corporate clients and financial sponsors achieve their financial and strategic objectives.
- Performing extensive financial statement modeling for a variety of transaction scenarios.
- Conducting comprehensive company and industry research.
- Analyzing financial model output and client information to prioritize data and present conclusions for discussion purposes.
- Coordinating with Managing Directors to provide indicative transaction structure and pricing guidance based on financial model and comparable transaction analysis.
- Preparing pitch materials for client meetings.
- Supporting Portfolio / Relationship Managers in transaction screening and credit / underwriting approval meetings to provide detailed overviews on clients and transactions and offer market insights and advice.
- Playing a key leadership role throughout the transaction execution process.
- Participating in accounting, business, and legal due diligence (with drafting sessions for public offerings).
- Working with legal counsel and clients / financial sponsors to draft and negotiate all legal documentation.
- Working with sales distribution team to develop syndication strategies with targeted investor lists and populate and manage data room information and access.
- Preparing detailed transaction marketing materials including confidential information memoranda and lender presentations.
- Organizing Ratings Agency Meetings, Lender meetings and Investor Roadshows for private and public debt offerings.
- Coordinating with sales distribution team to answer lender due diligence questions.
- Assisting clients, internal operations team, and investors through the closing process.

Qualifications, Education, Certifications and/or Other Professional Credentials
Required:
- We seek multi-faceted, results-driven, creative individuals ideally with 4+ years experience in Investment Banking or in the Big 4 Deals Advisory practice, who can generate ideas and execute them successfully as part of a dynamic team.
- Bachelors Degree in Finance or related field
Preferred:

- You will need to demonstrate superior problem solving and analytical capabilities accompanied by evidence of academic excellence and a strong work ethic.
- You should have a track record of showing leadership and teamwork aptitudes, as well as display exceptional written and oral communication skills.
- A strong attention to detail and focus on quality of client deliverables is essential.

This senior level performer will have an immediate impact. We reward you with an uncapped incentive opportunity and the ability to grow your career with a world class organization.

Primary responsibilities include
- Develop consultative relationships with small business clients in your target market with annual revenues ranging from one million to ten million dollars.
- Understand the client needs, provide value added solutions, manage a portfolio of existing customers and drive new commercial customer relationships.
- Partner effectively with an award-winning business banking team offering a wide array of product solutions that will enable you to enhance the customer experience, increase loyalty and improve the profitability of customer and the Bank
- Complete Business Banking University and Drive Sales training in your initial four-week orientation and a commercial credit training program to insure you’re prepared to identify, assess and mitigate lending risk.
- Maintain strong market knowledge and develop, retain and expand relationships with Centers of Influence i.e. CPA’s and Attorneys.
- Actively engage in significant community activity to expand potential customer base.

Qualifications, Education, Certifications and/or Other Professional Credentials
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience, required.
- 2+ years in a Business Banking Relationship Manager role or related business lending experience preferred.
- Business to Business sales experience required.
- Motivated self-starter with demonstrated leadership ability and potential.
- Successfully operate in a “team” atmosphere building upon and leveraging strong internal and external network.
- Ability to succeed in a fast paced, demanding sales culture with measured routines and goals aimed at new loan and deposit generation, cross sales, customer service and satisfaction
- Proficiency with portfolio/account management preferred.
- Ability to understand core business products and services. Consistent record of sales and outside calling skills.
- Excellent communication (written & verbal) and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to develop strong customer and colleague relationships.

Hours and Work Schedule
- Hours per Week: 40
- Work Schedule: Monday - Friday

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager (GCC Transfer Phase)
jobs.description:
Senior Program Manager, GCC Transfer Phase
Location and Work Model
Four day onsite hybrid schedule in one of the following Citizens hubs:
• Johnston, RI
• Phoenix, AZ
• Westwood or Medford, MA
• Iselin, NJ
• Pittsburgh, PA
• Franklin, TN
• Cleveland, OH
• Chicago, IL
Role Summary
The Senior Program Manager, GCC Transfer Phase leads the final stage of Citizens Global Capability Center journey, executing the transition of vendor delivered services and resources into CFG India under the Build Operate Transfer model.
This role is accountable for large scale workforce, service, and operational transfers across geographies, ensuring seamless delivery continuity, strong employee retention, and successful transition to a fully owned CFG India operating model.
This is a mission critical leadership role requiring deep experience in GCC transformations, BOT transfer execution, and complex multi vendor program delivery, with a strong focus on execution discipline, risk management, and business outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Program Leadership
• Lead end to end transfer execution, including planning, delivery, and stabilization across multiple waves
• Own the integrated roadmap, milestones, dependencies, and critical path from vendor state to CFG India ownership
• Ensure alignment to GCC objectives, including service continuity, knowledge retention, and minimal disruption
Vendor to Colleague Transition
• Drive transition of vendor resources into CFG India colleagues, including rebadging, onboarding, and integration
• Partner with vendors to validate workforce data, compensation alignment, and transfer readiness
• Establish knowledge transfer frameworks to prevent capability loss and ensure continuity
Cross Functional Execution
• Coordinate across ETS, CFG India leadership, HR, Total Rewards, Legal, Finance, Risk, and vendor partners
• Ensure alignment across key pillars
• Talent acquisition and onboarding
• Compensation, payroll, and statutory readiness
• Technology platforms and environment transition
• Change management and communications
Governance, Risk, and Control
• Establish and manage governance frameworks specific to transfer execution
• Identify and mitigate risks related to retention, service quality, knowledge gaps, and vendor dependency
• Ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and transfer pricing requirements
Executive Stakeholder Management
• Serve as primary transfer program lead, providing updates and recommendations to executive stakeholders
• Drive alignment across senior leaders in the United States and India
• Lead governance forums, including readiness reviews and go or no go decisions
People, Change, and Culture
• Partner with HR and Change teams to drive employee acceptance and retention
• Lead communication strategies to support workforce transition and cultural integration
• Preserve institutional knowledge and critical talent continuity
Stabilization and Optimization
• Oversee post transfer stabilization and hypercare
• Ensure delivery meets SLA and KPI expectations
• Drive continuous improvement and productivity optimization
Required Qualifications
• 10 plus years of program or project management experience
• 7 plus years leading large scale global transformation programs
• Direct experience with GCC or captive buildouts and BOT transfer execution
• Proven track record in vendor transition, workforce migration, and service transformation
• Experience working within multi vendor environments such as Infosys or Cognizant
• Strong expertise in governance, risk management, and executive stakeholder engagement
• Experience across full lifecycle programs including Build, Operate, and Transfer
Hours and Schedule
• 40 hours per week
• Monday through Friday
Pay Transparency
The salary range for this position is from $175,000 to $255,000 per year, plus an opportunity to earn an annual discretionary bonus. Actual pay is based on various factors including but not limited to, the budget, work location, relevant skills, and experience.
We offer competitive pay, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, retirement benefits, maternity and paternity leave, flexible work arrangements, education reimbursement, wellness programs, and more. Citizens’ paid time off policy exceeds the mandatory paid sick or paid time away policies of local and state jurisdictions in the United States. For an overview of our benefits, visit our Careers site - https://jobs.citizensbank.com/benefits.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager (GCC Operate Phase)
jobs.description:
Senior Program Manager - Global Capabilities Center (Operate Phase)
Location and Work Model
This role requires a four day on site, one remote hybrid work schedule in one of the following organizational hubs
• Johnston, RI
• Phoenix, AZ
• Westwood or Medford, MA
• Plano, TX
• Iselin, NJ
• Pittsburgh, PA
• Franklin, TN
• Cleveland, OH
• Chicago, IL
Role Focus: GCC Operate Phase Program Oversight
The Senior Program Manager for GCC Operate Phase is responsible for ensuring the ongoing consistency, and operational maturity of Citizens Global Capability Center for the Operate phase.
This role is responsible for the end-to-end program governance, buildout, and operational oversight of the Operate Phase within the Global Capability Center (GCC). This role partners closely with enable the broader GCC and enterprise global strategy. The Operate Phase focuses on stabilizing and scaling operations by implementing the full global operating model, ensuring consistent service delivery, and meeting defined SLAs and KPIs.
This phase includes end-to-end talent management, governance oversight, vendor management, and execution of core support functions. It also drives continuous improvement.
Key Responsibilities:
Operate phase Program Leadership
•    Provide strategic program leadership for GCC Operate Phase focused on the operating model optimization, communications, vendor oversight, and enablement of the global operating model.
•    Establish and manage an integrated program roadmap aligned to GCC maturity stages (startup, scale, optimize, transform).
•    Drive consistency in operating models, controls, governance, and service delivery across enabling functions.
Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management
•    Act as a central point of coordination between ETS, GCC leadership, and service providers for the Operate Phase.
•    Facilitate executive-level updates, steering committees, and decision forums related to the operate phase.
•    Drive alignment across global and regional stakeholders with competing priorities and dependencies.
Transformation & Continuous Improvement
•    Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and scalability through process re-engineering, automation, and digitization.
•    Support enterprise transformation initiatives impacting the operate phase, including system implementations, policy changes, and operating model shifts.
•    Promote standardization and adoption of best practices across the GCC ecosystem.
Financial & Resource Management
•    Support business case development for new services, expansions, or transformation initiatives.
•    Optimize resource utilization across internal teams and external partners.
Required Qualifications:
Experience
•    10+ years of experience in program management, operations, or shared services within large, complex enterprises.
•    Demonstrated experience supporting or leading large programs with having GCC Build-Operate-Transfer expertise or M&A expertise as a plus
•    Proven track record managing large-scale, cross-functional programs and/or GCC or shared services environments.
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Engineering, Information Technology, Operations Management, or a related field required. • Master's degree (MBA or related advanced degree) preferred.
Skills & Competencies:
•    Strong program and portfolio management expertise
•    Deep understanding of enterprise governance, risk management, and compliance principles.
•    Exceptional stakeholder management and executive communication skills.
•    Strong analytical, financial, and problem-solving capabilities.
•    Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-evolving environments.
Hours and Schedule
• 40 hours per week
• Monday through Friday
Pay Transparency
The salary range for this position is $175,000 to $250,000 per year, plus an opportunity to earn additional incentive earnings. Actual pay is based on various factors including, but not limited to, the budget, work location, and relevant skills and experience.
Benefits
Comprehensive benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, retirement plans, parental leave, flexible work arrangements, education reimbursement, wellness programs, and generous paid time off exceeding local requirements.

jobs.title: Fraud Operations Lead- ID Theft
jobs.description:
As a part of our team, you’re made ready for a fulfilling career with exciting new challenges and opportunities to stretch yourself!
As the Fraud Operations Lead for the ID theft team , you will require expertise in a variety of work processes through a combination of job-related training and considerable on-the-job experience. More specifically, you will be responsible for taking calls from customers and collecting, reviewing, responding, and analyzing data and/or documentation to ensure compliance with department SLAs, policies, procedures, and/or regulatory and risk requirements in a fast-paced environment.  This position requires the application of various methods, procedures, and knowledge of the business unit’s product(s) and system application(s). You will also perform routine, analytical review of data and/ or documentation which may include customer data and/or review for fraud/risk activities, and you may participate in projects requiring coordination with other teams and managing competing priorities in an accurate and timely manner.
Most importantly, you’ll experience new things, create new opportunities, think beyond your role, and make an impact!
Primary responsibilities include
- Responsible for preventing losses to Citizens and/or bank customers through fraud detection or fraud claims processing.
- Responds to and resolves escalated inquiries/problems from staff, internal and external clients.
- Take inbound calls from customers.
- Provide mentoring to colleagues in policies and procedures for the area/workflow.

Qualifications, Education, Certifications and/or Other Professional Credentials
- Required Qualifications - High School Graduate or Equivalent Required
- At least 2 years Banking Experience, Fraud experience preferred
- Ability to remain organized in a fast paced environment
- Demonstrated ability to multi-task
- Ability to work independently or in a team environment
- Impeccable customer services skills
- Proficiency in PC skills and MS Office
- Solid analytical skills
- High attention to detail
- Associates Degree preferred

Hours & Work Schedule
- Hours per Week:  40
- Work Schedule: Monday -Friday 8am-430pm  4 days in office at the  Pittsburgh, PA or Johnston RI locations, 1 day from home
